metadata.note: The Tyrone and Clearfield Railroad (chartered 1854; foreclosed 1867 and reorganised as the Tyrone and Clearfield Railway), run by the Pennsylvania Railroad as its 'Tyrone & Clearfield Branch' from Vail (on the Bald Eagle Valley, 3.1 mi from Tyrone) via Osceola Mills and Philipsburg to Clearfield, Curwensville and Grampian, with the Moshannon Branch (Osceola Mills - Houtzdale - Ramey - Madera - McCartney) and the Morrisdale, Little Muddy Run and Banian branches. The PRR leased the road 'from the beginning of operation' (2 Jul 1862) and ran every passenger train, so there is no ownership split (Rule 4): every feature is company 'Pennsylvania Railroad'. One feature per drawable span: the main stem is three features because its three sections have different confirmed start years. Research report: research/branches/tyrone_and_clearfield_railroad.txt.

not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] start, Moshannon Branch Osceola Mills - Ramey: 1879 (Nov 1879 card) is the first confirmed year; the Osceola - Moshannon Creek stub dates from the T&C era (pre-1867) and Houtzdale was a borough by 1872, so an earlier start is likely but unproven.

[OPEN] start, Philipsburg - Morrisdale: 1879 is the first confirmed year; earlier start unproven. Its end is drawn to 1904 (last confirmed) though PRRL brackets the discontinuance 11/1904 - 11/28/1906.

[ANCHOR] Ramey - Madera 1932, Madera - McCartney 1927, Banian Jct - Chesterfield 1909: single proven years from PRRL; start dates not found. Next step: Clearfield Republican / Raftsman's Journal PRR timetable adverts of the 1880s-1900s on Chronicling America (the Nov 1879 card is the template) or ICC valuation records.

Curwensville - Grampian: the extension's opening year is unknown (after Nov 1879); the 1916 start rests on a single Railway Mail Service mention. Fallback if not accepted as passenger proof: 1939-1939 [ANCHOR].
Little Muddy Run (Smoke Run - Almaden): drawn 1923-1924 only; PRRL has two entries that disagree - 'Ramey-Fernwood (9/28/24-4/28/29)' and '_____-Almaden 7/9/1932? (g)'. Start before 1923 not found.

1862-1863 passenger service on the Tyrone - Sandy Ridge - Powelton stub: line open (Jan/Jul 1862) and freight ran, but no passenger timetable before Nov 1864 was found; Raftsman's Journal 1862-64 only partly searched.
Philipsburg opening: WIKI 21 Oct 1863 vs PAG 'not opened for business until January 1, 1864' (Osceola). Immaterial to the 1864 drawn start.

Curwensville in the Feb 1952 Guide index reads 'Pennsylvania, 106' with no visible freight-only dagger while every other table-106 station is daggered; table 106 is missing from the scan. Treated as OCR loss; if table 106 is found with passenger times, the 1942 end would be wrong.
Headways and avg_speed_kmh are estimates throughout; only the 1864 (one round trip) and 1879 (two each way) service levels are sourced.

Geometry: Morrisdale Branch - Fowler's Loch Lomond Jct does not fit the mapped PRR 'Philipsburg Branch' that is drawn (trace 3.8 mi vs 3.3 documented); the passenger route may have run differently. Moshannon Branch Osceola Mills - Houtzdale traces 0.7 mi short of Fowler.
PRRL is a compiled secondary list (PRRTHS 2003), not a primary timetable, and is the only source for every end date.

segments.note: Pennsylvania Railroad, lessee "from the beginning of operation" (lease 2 Jul 1862, WIKI) - the Tyrone and Clearfield company never ran its own trains, and its 1867 foreclosure/reorganisation as the Tyrone and Clearfield Railway changed only the paper owner. Start: the earliest CONFIRMED passenger year is 1864 - Raftsman's Journal, 30 Nov 1864, prints a dated timetable, one round trip Tyrone 8:55 a.m. - Philipsburg 11:00 a.m., returning 3:50 p.m. (RJ64; the same standing card Apr 1865, RJ65). The track was open to Sandy Ridge Jan 1862, Powelton Jul 1862 and Philipsburg 21 Oct 1863 (WIKI; PAG says Osceola was 'not opened for business until January 1, 1864' - a conflict recorded, immaterial to the 1864 start), but no passenger train on the 1862-63 stub has been found (RJ62 is a freight notice), so 1862-63 is NOT drawn. By the 10 Nov 1879 card two daily-except-Sunday trains each way, the Clearfield Mail and Clearfield Express, ran Tyrone - Clearfield (CR80). End: last train Vail - Philipsburg - Curwensville 20 Oct 1942 (PRRTHS discontinuance list, starred 'believed correct'). Freight (coal) continued; Osceola Mills - Vail was abandoned c.1968 (CCE). Headway is an estimate (one round trip in 1864, two in 1879; nothing later read).

Headway not sourced beyond the 1864 and 1879 cards.

segments.note: Pennsylvania Railroad throughout (see the Vail - Philipsburg feature). Start: the Clearfield Republican of 10 Nov 1869 reports 'the passenger coach attached to the Clearfield freight train which has been running between this place and Philipsburg for about two months' - a MIXED train from about Sept 1869, which counts as passenger service (CR69). The line reached Clearfield in 1869 (CCE, WIKI). Full passenger trains, the Clearfield Mail and Clearfield Express, by Nov 1879 (CR80). End: last train Vail - Philipsburg - Curwensville 20 Oct 1942 (PRRL, starred). Parallels the NYC Beech Creek line Wallaceton - Woodland - Clearfield (separate track, separate stations; beech_creek_railroad.geojson). Headway is an estimate (one mixed train in 1869, two each way in 1879).

segments.note: Pennsylvania Railroad throughout. Start: the extension was 'finished to within the neighborhood of Curwensville' when an inspection special ran over it in Nov 1874 (CR74 - not public service), and the 1911 county history says 'opened for traffic in 1874' (an opening, not a passenger date). Through trains Tyrone - Curwensville in Nov 1879 (CR80). End: 'Vail-Philipsburg-Curwensville 10/20/1942' (PRRL, starred). The Feb 1952 Guide index shows Curwensville under PRR table 106 with no visible freight-only dagger while its neighbours are daggered - treated as OCR loss, not as evidence of service after 1942 (see not_yet_sourced). segments.note: Pennsylvania Railroad. Start: the extension's opening year is NOT SOURCED (it is not on the Nov 1879 card, CR80; Grampian got a new station in 1892, W2K, and was 'the present terminus of the Tyrone & Clearfield Branch' in 1911, PAG - neither is passenger proof). The earliest CONFIRMED year is 1916: the Harrisburg Telegraph of 10 Jun 1916 mentions 'a mail clerk running between Tyrone and Grampian' - a Railway Mail Service route, i.e. a mail train through to Grampian. That PRR branch mail trains carried passengers is an INFERENCE; if a reviewer will not accept an RPO route as passenger proof, fall back to 1939-1939 [ANCHOR]. Service certainly began earlier than 1916, but no earlier year is confirmed - do not extend without evidence. End: last passenger run Curwensville - Grampian 29 Apr 1939 (PRRL, starred), three years before the rest of the branch; freight-only by 1951 (Feb 1952 Guide index, Grampian daggered). Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Pennsylvania Railroad. [OPEN] START: 1879 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start - the PRR card effective Monday 10 Nov [1879] (Clearfield Republican, Mar 1880) has a 'Philipsburg & Moshannon Branches' table with times through Osceola, Moshannon, Sterling, Houtzdale, McCauley and Kendrick's to Ramey (CR80). An earlier start is likely - the first 4.5 mi from Osceola Mills is a Tyrone and Clearfield-era line (WIKI) and Houtzdale was a borough by 1872 - but no earlier passenger evidence was found. Do not extend without evidence. A 1931 Moshannon Branch timetable still listed the Osceola Mills (Mill Street) stop (W2K). End: 'Osceola Mills-Madera 7/8/1932 (last)' (PRRL, starred). Freight to Conrail; the corridor has been the Houtzdale Line Trail since 1994. Headway is an estimate.
